claim_reviews.rationale: Sutton describes stone-sided artery and branch furrows, sub-furrows along contours and groups of stone-divided cultivation plots. Does not independently date the contextual interval.

Stump 2024 explicitly associates first abandonment and cessation with likely eighteenth or early nineteenth century and reports present irrigation. The range is a broad approximate operational interpretation, not a precise source boundary; Sutton independently confirms old system abandoned by his survey, not the specific date or cessation. Scope and caveats confine the event to historical sediment capture.

The 2017 paper estimates over 1,000 ha and interprets section 11 wall 4005 as later used alongside canal 4247, whose fill was cut for narrower canal 4050. Layers 4041 and 4048 are interpreted as deliberate accumulations after abandonment of the later canal. The date is publication, not construction.
sources: w12-lang-stump-engaruka: Abstract; Results, Stratigraphy, Fig. 4; Discussion

claim_reviews.rationale: The paper contextualizes the landscape as 15th–18th century, describes a relative stratigraphic sequence and asks for better absolute dates; identity and causes are not fixed by these sources.
Relative chronology, field-date limitations and unsettled causes are clearly described as open questions; proposed evidence is future research rather than a historical assertion.

The unqualified discovery-wide value abandoned covers the named combined irrigation and sediment-capture practice. Stump says irrigation continues, although deliberate sediment capture ceased at first abandonment. Remove fate and research.basis.fate; keep the specifically scoped abandonment event and caveat. A discovery-wide fate may be reconsidered if the record is explicitly narrowed with adequate evidence.
